prompt: Economic progress is one way to measure the success of a country, while some people think there are other factors. What other factors should be considered? Within these factors, do you think anything is more important than economic progress?
essay:
Many countries consider economic progress to be the leading factor in indicating their success, while there are more factors that are considered in highly developed countries, such as educational level, government policies, and infrastructure. Out of these contributors, I believe that the provision of welfare systems is the most significant.

First of all, one of the main factors of a highly developed country is a high-quality education system. After finishing their well-rounded education and training in school, companies and governments can recruit intelligent and well-educated students to develop a qualified and skilled workforce. This cycle allows workers to contribute their professional skills and abilities to improve economic development and boost productivity. Besides, providing regular free health check-ups for the public can also foster residents’ healthy lifestyles. This policy can bring about beneficial results, leading to healthier populations that support the country’s development.

Another indicator is well-developed infrastructure in cities and rural areas. When people can use public amenities, transportation, and open spaces, such as public gardens and parks, regardless of location, citizens may live a high-quality life and experience satisfaction with their country, which is highly linked to a country’s success. Hence, governments in successful countries evenly distribute tax funding to develop both rural and urban areas and reduce the gap. As a result, people are also willing to move and live in the countryside instead of being fully packed in cities that create intense competition.

Among the factors that are considered to define a well-developed country, I believe that the provision of welfare systems is of the utmost importance. In fact, social safety nets are highly correlated with a high score on the World Happiness Index. In social democratic societies in Northern Europe, such as Iceland and Finland, the government spends tax money to provide affordable education and healthcare, paid leave, well-developed facilities, and retirement funding. As a result, citizens are more likely to be family-oriented, maintain a healthy work-life balance, and be more satisfied with their lives.

In conclusion, there are various indicators that are considered when defining a well-developed country, including advanced infrastructure, policies, and educational equality. I believe that the most important factor is high-quality security nets, as government tax revenue can be used effectively in increasing the life satisfaction of a populace.
